                      Hyperspectral imagery denoising via reweighed sparse low-rank
                                   nonnegative tensor factorization

                                                     Fengchao Xiong1   Jun Zhou2   Yuntao Qian1

                                                                                                                1                                                                                           College of Computer Science, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China
                                                                                                 2                                                                         School of Information and Communication Technology, Griﬃth University, Nathan, Australia

,
 Introduction

 In this paper, a reweighed sparse low-rank nonnegative tensor factorization (RSLRNTF) method is proposed to restore an HSI. It takes an HSI as a third-order tensor and factorizes it into the combination of a few
 component tensors where each one is the outer product of a low-rank matrix (coding matrix) and a vector (atom). A reweighed L1 norm is added to coding matrices to enforce their sparsity. The low-rankness in
 both spatial and spectral domain is in line with the spatial and spectral correlation in an HSI. Furthermore, we add nonnegativity constraint to both coding coeﬃcients matrices and dictionary to learn parts-based
 representation of HSI, which facilitates preserving local structure information.
